published.title: Bridge and torch (4 people, 17 min)
published.answer: 17: A+Z cross (2), A back (1), Omar+Grandad cross (10), Z back (2), A+Z cross (2)

published.title: Two doors, one lion; Person 1 always tells the truth, Person 2 always lies; one question to one guard
published.answer: Ask either guard: 'If I asked the other guard which door leads outside, which door would he point to?' Then take the OTHER door. (Truth-teller reports the liar's lie; liar lies about the truth-teller's answer: both point to the lion door.)

published.title: The broken vase: heavy rain all morning; Person 1 reading in the garden, Person 2 baking in the kitchen, Person 3 asleep upstairs
published.answer: Person 1. It had been raining heavily since sunrise, so nobody could have been reading in the garden the whole time (and the book is perfectly dry).

published.title: Three boxes (apples, oranges, mixed); Person 1 got every label wrong; take one fruit from one box without looking, then fix all three labels
published.answer: Box 3, the one labelled MIXED. Its label is wrong, so it holds only one kind. If you pull an apple, it is the apples box; the box labelled ORANGES can't be oranges (wrong label) and can't be apples, so it's mixed; the box labelled APPLES is oranges. (Same logic the other way round if you pull an orange.)

published.title: Three light switches, one lamp in another room behind a closed door; flip switches freely, but open the door only once (Person 1 sets the rule)
published.answer: Turn switch 1 on for a few minutes, then turn it off. Turn switch 2 on and open the door. Lamp lit = switch 2; lamp off but warm = switch 1; lamp off and cold = switch 3.

published.title: Boil an egg for exactly 9 minutes; no clock, no phone; only a 4-minute and a 7-minute sand timer (Person 1)
published.answer: Start both timers when the egg goes in. At 4 min the 4-timer runs out: flip it. At 7 min the 7-timer runs out: flip it (the 4-timer has 1 min left). At 8 min the 4-timer runs out: flip the 7-timer again; it has only 1 min of sand on top, so it runs out at exactly 9 min.

published.title: Wolf, goat and cabbage: Person 1 must take all three across a river; the boat holds Person 1 + only one thing; left alone, the wolf eats the goat and the goat eats the cabbage
published.answer: Take the goat over. Come back alone. Take the wolf over, and bring the goat back. Take the cabbage over (it stays with the wolf). Come back alone. Take the goat over. (Taking the cabbage first and bringing the goat back works too.)

published.title: Two fathers and two sons go fishing and catch exactly three fish; each takes home one whole fish, nobody shares
published.answer: There are only three people: a grandfather, his son and his grandson. The grandfather and the father are the two fathers; the father and the grandson are the two sons. Three people, three fish.

published.title: Clock tower: strikes 6 times in exactly 5 seconds (instant strikes, equal gaps; Person 1 counts); how long to strike 12 times?
published.answer: 11 seconds. 6 strikes have 5 gaps, so each gap is 1 second. 12 strikes have 11 gaps = 11 seconds (not 10).
